title: How an Oven Thermostat Works in 60 Seconds 🌡️🔥 #shorts
description:
Your oven never holds one exact temperature. A sensor probe inside measures the heat, and the control switches the heating element on below your setting and off just above it. The result is a gentle wave of temperature around the number you picked. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#oven #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Your oven never holds one temperature. It *clicks on and off* the whole time.

steps.label: Sensor
steps.text: A metal *sensor probe* sits inside, measuring the hot air.

steps.label: Resistance
steps.text: As it heats up, its electrical *resistance* rises, so the control can read the temperature.

steps.label: Heat on
steps.text: Below your setting, a switch sends power, and the *heating element* glows.

steps.label: Heat off
steps.text: Just past the target, it *cuts the power*, and the oven slowly cools.

steps.label: Cycle
steps.text: Then it heats again, so the temperature *waves* up and down around your number.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Sense, switch, *repeat*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
